environment.description: AWS Lambda function deployed with identical code, but fronted by a CloudFront distribution (ID: E2XYZABC123) configured with Origin Access Control (OAC) policy (signing behavior: always, origin type: Lambda function URL). The Lambda function URL auth-type is set to AWS_IAM, meaning only requests signed with SigV4 by the CloudFront OAC principal are accepted. Direct invocation of the Lambda function URL without valid CloudFront signature returns 403. Additionally, the CloudFront distribution has a custom origin request policy (ID: 88a5eaf4-2fd4-4709-b370-b4c650ea3fcf) that strips and rewrites the 'url' query parameter through a CloudFront Function (viewer-request stage) which performs URL canonicalization and blocks any request where the decoded 'url' parameter contains RFC 1918 addresses, link-local ranges (169.254.x.x), or schemes other than https://. The CloudFront Function uses a compiled regex pattern matching against the fully-decoded (up to 3 rounds of percent-decoding) URL parameter value. The function also rejects requests where the 'url' parameter hostname resolves via DNS to any non-routable IP (DNS resolution performed at edge via CloudFront Function's built-in net.resolve()). Lambda execution role has no VPC attachment in this configuration, running in default Lambda networking (AWS-managed ENI, no direct metadata endpoint access).

config.origin_access_control: OAC with SigV4 signing, always sign
config.cloudfront_function: viewer-request URL canonicalization and SSRF filter
config.cf_function_behavior: 3-round percent-decode, block RFC1918/link-local/non-https, DNS resolution check
